title: Faster around the circle
hook: Change orbital speed and predict centripetal acceleration.
misconception: centripetal acceleration doubles when orbital speed doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply a_c = v²/r to compare centripetal acceleration when orbital speed changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With uniform circular motion with fixed radius, a_c = v²/r. When orbital speed doubles, centripetal acceleration becomes 4 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model a_c = v²/r; scaling exponent 2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider uniform circular motion with fixed radius, with a nonzero initial result. If orbital speed triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on centripetal acceleration?
recall.why: Apply a_c = v²/r under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 9.
